title: Harmonize client initialization patterns and steward dependency upgrades across Python/JS/Go SDKs
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Summary: We will standardize the client initialization surface across Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs and perform a coordinated dependency upgrade wave to reduce transitive risk, simplify onboarding, and eliminate multiple legacy init patterns that increase cognitive load and bugs. This ticket coordinates API compatibility, deprecation warnings, testing, and rollout.

Motivation: Over the last 18 months each language client has drifted: different env var precedence, inconsistent token/credential passing (env -> config -> explicit param), and divergent default transports. These differences increase support load and cause subtle user errors when teams switch languages or copy code samples. Additionally, several transitive dependencies (http libraries, crypto utils) are behind supported versions and contain performance and security patches.

Scope:
- Define a single canonical initializer pattern (Client.from_env / Client.from_config + explicit Client(options)) and implement in Python, JS, Go.
- Add graceful deprecation warnings for legacy constructors (maintain backwards-compat for two minor releases).
- Bump key runtime dependencies across SDKs (requests/httpx -> latest LTS; node-fetch/undici -> LTS; go-http-client deps) and harmonize supported TLS/cipher defaults.
- Audit and remove polyfills/compat shims that are no longer required (node: buffer shims, py: compat layer for py2-era code).
- Add CI compatibility matrix tests for all three clients to validate init surfaces and env precedence.
- Run perf regression benchmarks and revert any dep that causes >5% throughput/latency regression without mitigation.
- Publish migration guide and update quickstarts, examples, and SDK docs.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Backwards-compat: We will keep legacy constructors but emit explicit deprecation warnings and document migration steps. This reduces churn for customers but requires additional testing and interim code paths.
- Dep bump strategy: prefer LTS versions and minimal surface changes. If a dependency bump introduces breaking behavior (e.g., transport timeouts), evaluate a small shim or opt-in config flag for a single release cycle.
- Performance: prioritize throughput in Python and latency in JS for browser usage; if a dep bump causes regressions we will trial alternate libraries (e.g., undici vs node-fetch).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Specification: finalize canonical init API and env precedence doc (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Unified+Client+Init) — owner: Priya (done).
2) API adapters: implement the canonical constructors in each repo alongside legacy constructors that emit warnings (feature branch per language).
3) Dependency wave: compile a matrix of current versions and target LTS versions; open dep bump PRs grouped by library (transport, crypto, logging).
4) Tests & CI: add cross-language compatibility test harness that runs init permutations and asserts env precedence; add smoke tests for auth/kms flows.
5) Perf & security validation: run perf suite and SCA scan; log regressions and triage.
6) Docs & migration: write migration guide, update quickstarts, and prepare release notes.
7) Rollout: ship in sdk-2025.03 release; monitor errors and uptake for two weeks; stage removal of legacy constructors in sdk-2025.05.

Risks & mitigations:
- Breaking changes in 3rd-party libs: stage PRs, add integration tests, and hold on release if high-risk.
- Hidden usage patterns: provide opt-out flag and make deprecation warnings actionable (link to migration snippet).
- Performance regressions: benchmark and if >5% regression, revert or replace the dependency.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Python/JS/Go clients expose the canonical init patterns and legacy constructors emit deprecation warnings.
- CI matrix validates env precedence permutations for all languages.
- Key runtime deps bumped to targeted LTS versions (list in PRs) and SCA shows no high vulnerabilities.
- Perf benchmarks show <=5% regression per language compared to baseline; any regression mitigated or justified.
- Migration guide, quickstarts, and release notes published.
- Release sdk-2025.03 contains the changes and a roll-forward/rollback plan documented.

Next steps (short term):
- Marcelo to open language PR skeletons and draft deprecation message copy (due 2025-01-30).
- QA to define compatibility test permutations (due 2025-02-06).
- Security to run SCA on proposed dep matrix (due 2025-02-10).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical init API implemented in Python/JS/Go with documented examples.
Legacy constructors emit deprecation warnings and have automated tests asserting warnings appear.
Dependency versions updated in lockfiles/package manifests and linked PRs created.
CI compatibility matrix covering env, explicit params, and config precedence added.
Perf regression <5% or mitigations documented for any regressions discovered.
Migration guide and release notes published before sdk-2025.03 cut.
No critical/high SCA findings blocking release (or mitigations tracked).
